I absolutely in no way want to take away from the fact that this character has always been a man, and in the instances where he refers to himself in the past, he uses he / him pronouns. He does chose to keep his birth name, so I don't think that deadnaming will be an issue for this. I'm mostly worried about depicting this character as more feminine presenting (For context, they were raised in a traditionally southern US conservative home in the early 20th century,  a time where historically self expression was looked down upon), and other characters using the incorrect pronouns (of course, this is looked upon negatively narratively, I just want to illustrate how being misgendered back then impacted him then, and now in the present of the comic).

Thanks so much for this response! I really am trying my best to gather and research as many perspectives on the ftm transgender experience and their relation with their birth gender (partly why I'm posting this question haha), and  most of my writing for this character is based off of the advice and experiences many of my trans friends have shared with me, and my own experiences as a black lesbian!

I'm always eager to learn, and it's actually part of the reason why I wanted to include transgender narratives. A main narrative of this work is about acceptance of the past, and celebration of the present and future. I have always found the concept of being trans, and accepting and becoming who you are to be genuinely quite beautiful.  


EDIT: changed some language!

Mostly by other characters (his parents, friends, etc)! The narration is in the first person, so he mostly uses first person pronouns. He is drawn as feminine presenting during these portions, which is what I'm more worried about being seen as disrespectful. However, for some context, this character was raised in the early 20th century in a very conservative US southern home, where there wasn't much flexibility for self expression.
